learning_objective: The learner will examine a ten-row test data table and identify the five rows with errors and the kind of error in each, with at least 4 of 5 error rows named correctly on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** data-quality-detective
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine a ten-row test data table and identify the five rows with errors and the kind of error in each, with at least 4 of 5 error rows named correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Data Collection, Pre-Test, Post-Test, Learning Gain (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 16). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner marks each row Clean or Error, and for each Error row picks the kind of error. An error row is correct when both the marking and the kind match the Content table. Clean rows marked Error count against the learner. Mastery is at least 4 of the 5 error rows correct and no more than 1 clean row marked as an error, on the first attempt. Reading the error kinds is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A table that opens without a warning is correct. (2) A score of 120 belongs to a high-performing student. (3) A blank cell can be treated as zero. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a data table for errors is an Analyze-level action that comes before any calculation. A table with five different kinds of error and five clean rows teaches the learner to check each column against its meaning. **Content:** The data dictionary, shown at all times: Code (unique), Version (C or T), Pre-test (0 to 100), Post-test (0 to 100). The five kinds of error: Missing value, Out of range, Repeated code, Inconsistent label, Wrong unit. The ten rows (all made up): | Row | Code | Version | Pre-test | Post-test | Correct marking | Kind of error | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | S01 | T | 28 | 59 | Clean | None | The values are in range and the label is valid. | | 2 | S02 | C | 22 | 42 | Clean | None | The values are in range and the label is valid. | | 3 | S03 | T | 31 | (blank) | Error | Missing value | The post-test is blank, and a blank must not be treated as zero. | | 4 | S04 | C | 35 | 50 | Clean | None | The values are in range and the label is valid. | | 5 | S05 | T | 41 | 120 | Error | Out of range | A score of 120 is outside 0 to 100. | | 6 | S06 | C | 0.38 | 46 | Error | Wrong unit | The pre-test is a fraction and the column holds percentages. | | 7 | S07 | Treatment | 43 | 76 | Error | Inconsistent label | The column uses C and T, and this row uses a word. | | 8 | S08 | C | 45 | 64 | Clean | None | The values are in range and the label is valid. | | 9 | S08 | T | 47 | 70 | Error | Repeated code | Code S08 appears twice, so two students share a code. | | 10 | S10 | C | 48 | 66 | Clean | None | The values are in range and the label is valid. | **Provenance:** The rows are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The error kinds follow the chapter section "Data Collection". **Rules:** Exactly five rows are errors and five are clean. Each of the five kinds of error appears once. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the table and the data dictionary. 2. The learner marks each row Clean or Error, and for each Error row picks the kind of error. 3. The learner presses Check. 4. The sim shows which markings were correct, the kind of each error, and the Why text. **Feedback:** One check, after all ten rows are marked. Correct: "Correct: row [n], [kind]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. Row [n] is [marking], [kind]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 5 error rows correct, [m] clean rows marked as errors". When mastery is met it adds "You can check a table before you use it." Otherwise it lists the Why text of each missed row. **Starting State:** The table with all rows unmarked, and the data dictionary. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says to check for missing values, scores outside 0 to 100, repeated codes, and labels typed two ways. The sim adds a wrong-unit error.
